steps.say: These tumours are graded by how fast their cells divide, seen as a staining percentage. Slow ones are removed surgically, while fast undifferentiated ones need drugs first.
steps.tx: Grading by **Ki-67** (division marker) under **3 percent** (three percent) for G1, **3 to 20 percent** (three to twenty) for G2 and over **20 percent** (twenty) for G3 with **differentiation** (maturation grade) decides surgery against systemic therapy in these slow tumours.

steps.say: Fainting spells with sweating that vanish after eating sweets point to extra insulin. A supervised three-day fast with blood tests at collapse proves the tiny pancreatic tumour.
steps.tx: **Insulinoma** (insulin-secreting tumour) shows the **Whipple triad** (collapse, low sugar, relief with glucose) with glucose under **55 mg per dL** (fifty five), insulin over **3 microunits per mL** (three units) and C-peptide over **0.6 ng per mL** (zero point six) during a **supervised fast** (watched three-day fast) of **72-hour fast** (three days) duration.

vis.alt: Pancreas with a small tumour driving low sugar through brain and adrenaline symptoms relieved by eating.
vis.caption: Insulinoma: autonomous insulin secretion causing hypoglycaemia with Whipple triad relieved by glucose. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Ulcers that return despite treatment, with watery diarrhoea, come from excess gastrin. The tumours hide in a small triangle spanning the bile duct, duodenum and pancreatic neck.
steps.tx: **Gastrinoma triangle** (cystic-duct junction, duodenal sweep, pancreatic neck) harbours Zollinger-Ellison tumours needing surgery, with **secretin stimulation** (hormone provocation test) rise over **120 pg per mL** (one twenty) confirming **Zollinger-Ellison** (gastrin excess) disease with ulcers and diarrhoea needing lifelong acid control.

vis.alt: Triangle spanning bile duct, duodenum and pancreas marking gastrinoma sites with ulcers shown.
vis.caption: Gastrinoma triangle with duodenal and pancreatic sites, nodal spread and ulcer disease. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A faulty gene grows tumours in many glands at once. Children of carriers are screened from early childhood, and the tiny duodenal tumours are found by opening the bowel at surgery.
steps.tx: **MEN1** (multi-gland tumour gene) with **menin** (tumour suppressor) mutation needs surveillance from age **5** (five) for parathyroid, pituitary and pancreatic tumours, with **duodenotomy** (opening the duodenum) for multiple duodenal gastrinomas that scans frequently miss in this syndrome despite best imaging.

steps.say: Small silent tumours in the tail are shelled out or removed with part of the pancreas, keeping the spleen whenever the vessels allow. Head tumours need the full Whipple operation.
steps.tx: Small nonfunctional tumours under **2 cm** (two centimetres) in the body-tail get **enucleation** (shelling out) or spleen-preserving distal pancreatectomy, while head lesions need **Whipple** (pancreatic head removal) with full nodal clearance for cure in fit surgical patients everywhere possible today.

steps.say: Liver spots from these slow tumours are scooped out when nearly all can go, leaving the patient with hormones and targeted radiation for the rest. Most live many years after such surgery.
steps.tx: Liver metastases get parenchyma-sparing **debulking** (bulk removal) when over **90 percent** (ninety percent) of disease is resectable, combined with octreotide and peptide receptor **radionuclide therapy** (targeted radiation) for residual disease over many years of careful follow-up worldwide today onwards still.

steps.say: A special scan lights up tumours carrying the somatostatin receiver and predicts who benefits from targeted radiation. Tumours glowing on ordinary sugar scans behave aggressively and need chemotherapy.
steps.tx: **Gallium-68 DOTATATE PET** (receptor scan) stages **somatostatin-avid** (receiver-positive) disease via the **somatostatin receptor** (tumour receiver) and selects PRRT candidates, while **FDG** (sugar scan) avidity marks aggressive G3 tumours needing systemic chemotherapy first, with surgery reserved for carefully selected cases after a clear response.

steps.say: Rashes that migrate, endless watery diarrhoea and new diabetes each betray a different hormone tumour. Glucagonoma and VIPoma sit toward the tail, while somatostatinoma of the head or duodenum needs a Whipple.
steps.tx: **Glucagonoma** (sugar-raising tumour) with **necrolytic migratory erythema** (wandering rash), **VIPoma** (watery-diarrhoea tumour) with potassium loss, localise to body-tail resection with regional nodal clearance for cure, while **somatostatinoma** (multi-hormone blocker) with gallstones and diabetes usually sits in the head or duodenum and needs **Whipple** (pancreatic head removal) with nodal clearance for cure.
